payload.headline: Project lifecycle mostly complete but 4/7 checks failed due to supplier invoice and employee role issues
what_went_wrong: Supplier invoice (25650 NOK from Dorada SL) was registered via ledger voucher instead of proper /incomingInvoice endpoint, likely failing the supplier cost check (Check 3 or 4).
Carmen Rodríguez's role as 'director de proyecto' may not have been properly set — employee was found but no role/title field was explicitly set, possibly failing Check 3 or 5.
Ana García's timesheet used employee id 18663714 but Carmen's used 18663709 — need to verify these IDs match the correct employees with correct roles.
The /incomingInvoice endpoint schema was never resolved correctly; two failed attempts with wrong field names wasted calls and the fallback voucher approach did not satisfy the scoring check.
what_worked: Project created successfully with correct budget (384950 NOK), customer, and project manager linkage.
Client invoice created successfully via order → orderline → invoice flow (checks 1, 2, 7 passed).
what_to_try_next: Inspect /incomingInvoice schema carefully before calling it — use inspect_tripletex_endpoint first and map exact field names (likely 'vendor' or nested object structure) to properly register the 25650 NOK supplier cost.
After finding Carmen Rodríguez, explicitly set her employee title/role to 'Direktør' or project manager role via PUT /employee/{id} to satisfy role-based checks.
Verify employee IDs by searching with email filter (GET /employee?email=carmen.rodriguez@example.org) to confirm correct mapping before registering timesheets.
unnecessary_calls: POST /incomingInvoice with wrong 'supplier' field — should have inspected schema first before attempting
POST /incomingInvoice second attempt with 'supplierId' — still wrong, inspect_tripletex_endpoint should have been called between attempts
PUT /ledger/account/471342740 to configure bank account — likely not required for scoring and added an unnecessary call
